history.reason: Verified demand that goes beyond the card's signals (iFixit BES878 question with only a bare video link, plus several home-barista.com threads on the same cut-out). Answers are scattered across Breville's generic support page, forum anecdotes and JustAnswer. A diagnosis order with a warranty and repair-or-replace rule is a clear gain, and it sits in the focus cluster.

The diagnosis order can be built from supported claims. The US booklet gives the free checks: tank seated and above MIN, a descale, a 5-minute water-filter soak, RESET DEFAULTS, and the 60-second hot-water stop. It has no row for a cut-out with beeps; its only escalation is the thermal cut-out row. Breville's warranty page gives the claim process and exclusions. Owner and repair-shop reports point to the flow meter when the cut-out persists, and one owner saw a flow-control repair fail again after seven months. Gaps are recorded as unknown claims: the text of Breville's own support article, the US warranty length, the flow-meter part number and price, and repair costs. Without those the writer can't give a numeric repair-or-replace threshold. The rule has to stay qualitative (in warranty, claim it; out of warranty, get a quote and compare it with the price of the machine), unless a human supplies the article text and a quote.
